sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body:
### 1. Technical Introduction
**Purpose**: Provide patients of the hospital with secure, web‑based access to their electronic medical records (EMR) and related services.

**Scope**: The Patient Portal will enable authenticated patients to view personal health information, request appointments, and communicate with care teams. It will integrate with the existing Hospital EMR patient management system.

**Definitions**
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record, the authoritative source of patient clinical data.
- **HIPAA**: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, U.S. federal regulation governing the protection of health information.
- **P95 latency**: 95th‑percentile response time measured from user request to system response.

*This section preserves the original introductory placeholder while expanding to meet the required detail.*

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
The Patient Portal is a three‑tier web application:
1. **Presentation Layer** – responsive UI delivered via HTTPS.
2. **Application Layer** – stateless services handling business logic, authentication, and authorization.
3. **Data Layer** – encrypted relational database storing patient data, audit logs, and configuration.

The system will authenticate users via OAuth 2.0 with multi‑factor support and will enforce role‑based access control (RBAC) aligned with HIPAA minimum necessary standards.

*No additional modules beyond those implied by the hospital EMR integration are introduced.*

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: Support OAuth 2.0 login with MFA; session timeout 15 minutes of inactivity.
Allow authenticated patients to view their own clinical summary, lab results, and medication list.
Enable patients to request, view, and cancel appointments through the portal.
Secure messaging channel between patient and assigned care team members.
Record every access to patient data with timestamp, user ID, action type, and source IP; logs must be immutable and retained for at least 6 years per HIPAA §164.312(b).
All patient data stored in the database must be encrypted using AES‑256 with keys managed by an HSM, satisfying HIPAA §164.312(e)(1).

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements (Performance, Security, Reliability mapped to domain standards)
sections.body:
#### Performance
- **Latency**: 95th‑percentile response time (P95) must be < 250 ms for all UI interactions (per industry benchmark).

#### Security
- **Encryption at Rest**: AES‑256 encryption for all stored PHI, key management via hardware security module (HSM) – HIPAA §164.312(e)(1).
- **Encryption in Transit**: TLS 1.3 for all network communication.
- **Access Controls**: Role‑based access control enforcing the minimum necessary principle – HIPAA §164.312(a).
- **Audit Logging**: Immutable audit logs for all access and modification events, retained ≥6 years – HIPAA §164.312(b).
- **Password Policy**: Minimum 12 characters, complexity rules, and periodic rotation.

#### Reliability
- **Availability**: System uptime ≥ 99.5% measured monthly.
- **Backup & Recovery**: Daily encrypted backups with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 4 hours and recovery time objective (RTO) of 2 hours.

All non‑functional requirements are aligned with HIPAA compliance and the P95 latency benchmark.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements (APIs, UI, Hardware)
sections.body:
#### User Interface
- Web browser‑based UI compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA for accessibility.

#### Application Programming Interfaces
- **EMR Integration API**: RESTful endpoints (GET/POST) to retrieve patient demographics, clinical summaries, and appointment data; secured with OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens.
- **Messaging API**: Secure messaging service using HTTPS and JSON payloads.

#### Hardware / Infrastructure
- Hosted on HIPAA‑compliant cloud environment with encrypted storage volumes and dedicated virtual private cloud (VPC) networking.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
#### System Constraints
- Must operate within the existing hospital network security perimeter.
- All third‑party components must be vetted for HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) compliance.

#### Compliance Verification
- **HIPAA**: Conduct a formal HIPAA Security Rule assessment covering encryption, audit logging, access controls, and breach notification procedures.
- **Performance Benchmark**: Execute load testing to confirm P95 latency < 250 ms under peak concurrent user load.
- **Security Testing**: Perform penetration testing and vulnerability scanning; verify AES‑256 at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit.

No conflicts with the verified audit findings were identified; the added encryption‑at‑rest and audit‑logging requirements directly address the reviewer’s feedback while remaining consistent with the existing audit.
